_doc: Which supplier parts each head-carrier screw post is made of (Idle T-5bqc3m). Post positions are never typed: robot/body/neck-head/head_holes.py measures the bore of the named spacer / shim / terminal nut on its mesh in the shell-pass manifest (defined_holes.SHELL_PASS), where the supplier parts sit as supplied. group: screw family of the post; spacers / terminals / screws: manifest part names in post order; washers (camera): the supplier washers whose board-side face is the board's front face (the head seat); legacy_screws: manifest parts the generated screws replace; drop: supplier parts the printed features replace; head: standard and thread of the screw (dk / k / lengths from robot/body/checks/data/hardware.json screw_standards; compute: ISO 10642 M2.5 dk / k written here, assumption). compute: pressed 304 sleeve around the post, screw into the nut. camera (owner 2026-11-22: only catalogue hardware, printable and hand-assemblable): the 8 supplier F-F standoffs are replaced by a printed column (column.ro, column.height 4.97 = the standoff's 5 mm less 0.03 mm so the board face never overlaps the column in the fit check; the screw clamp closes it) on the carrier plate with a clearance bore (column.bore_dia); a catalogue M2 x 3 brass heat-set insert is pushed from the plate's rear face (before ROCK4D goes on) up to the bore's ledge; the insert's rear end is flush with the plate's rear face (the heated tip ends on that face), its front end on the column bore's ledge; the ISO 4762 M2 screw is driven from the camera front through board and column into it, the smallest standard length that reaches the 1 d reference with its point inside the insert. The ribs behind the plate keep a square window of half-width press_clear_mm round each insert axis free for the heated tip (rib ends cut square, no slivers). mic (owner 2026-11-22: one screw, a printed retention instead of the upper screw; T-5bqc3m review: every step by hand on the bench): the board sits on a printed wing of the carrier (wing.face_gap_mm behind its back face, wing.t_mm thick, top wing.top_z_mm, thinned to wing.taper_t_mm above wing.taper_z_mm where the head skin closes in); one catalogue M2 x 3 brass heat-set insert in a boss on the wing's skin side (boss.ro), pushed from the boss's free end (+x, carrier alone on the bench) up to a printed floor; the floor is as thick as the screw needs: the insert's front end goes where the standard screw length reaches engagement_target_mm (the smallest length that leaves a floor of at least floor_min_mm), the insert's rear end is the boss end. The ISO 7380-1 M2 button head (k 1.3, clear of ROCK4D; a pan head k 1.6 would leave 0.1 mm) is driven from the board side through the PCB and the floor's clearance bore (bore_dia) before ROCK4D goes on, so mic and cable are fitted before the skin. A printed locating pin (pin.dia, pin.length into the PCB) on the wing face goes into the board's second mounting hole (the bore of drop[1]) and keeps it from turning about the screw; port: the acoustic port relief through the wing (robot/model/build/contracts.py microphone_port). Insert: catalogue-class brass knurled heat-set insert M2 x 3.0 mm, knurl OD 3.6 mm, recommended hole 3.2 mm (CNC Kitchen / Ruthex M2 x 3 class; ASSUMPTION: no supplier data in the repo, hole size from the manufacturers' published tables, not checked against a data sheet here); modelled as a tube of the hole diameter (sleeve.ro) with the thread's minor diameter as bore (no overlap check against the melted-in plastic). threads: ISO 724 M2 major / minor diameter (same values as torso_screws.THREADS). ASSUMPTIONS: thread modelled at the minor diameter; 1 d engagement for a steel screw in a brass thread (robot/actuators/interfaces/standard-parts.json lists 1.5 d for brass: 3.0 mm, the insert's length).

threads._doc: ISO 724 M2: major 2.0, minor 1.567 (the threaded sleeve's modelled bore); same as torso_screws.THREADS (T-bv7bwe). Assumption: no supplier data for M2 threaded press-in sleeves in the repo.
